title: [CQ-RF06b] VS Code protected daemon spawn
description:
Objective: under the protected profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension. This mirrors JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedDaemonCommand / protectedDaemonEnvironment / protectedCommandOrRefuse. Split out of CQ-RF06 (task-98ffe33f448746e6bc802db0b5624fd0) by architect-bd1eb82d on 2026-10-30 to keep each diff under the 400-LOC review cap. RF06 lands the shared policy as exported functions in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: runtimeProfile (strict, fail-closed, session pin), comparablePath/isWithin, installedRoot(extensionPath) = <extensionPath>/bundled and installedArtifact. This row consumes them in the same file.

Deliverable: when runtimeProfile(projectPath) is 'protected', MoeDaemonClient.startDaemon:
1. Selects the daemon with installedArtifact(installedRoot, 'daemon/index.js', projectPath). resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath and any project copy are never consulted.
2. Selects node as an absolute, real, regular file outside the project (a mirror of JetBrains installedExecutable). It tries, in this order:
   - MOE_NODE_COMMAND;
   - on non-Windows, ~/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node;
   - an in-process lookup of node or node.exe over PATH entries that are absolute and outside the project (never a bare name resolved by spawn);
   - on Windows, the resolveNodeExecutable candidates (ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nodejs, LOCALAPPDATA\nvm\current, APPDATA\nvm).
3. Spawns [node, daemon, 'start', '--project', projectPath] with cwd = the installed daemon's directory. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH (matched case-insensitively on Windows) keeps only absolute entries outside the project.
4. Refuses instead of falling back: any rejection starts nothing, logs the reason and shows `Protected execution profile: <reason>. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.`
5. The legacy profile is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Out of scope:
- Running-daemon provenance (JetBrains activationRefusal, spawn records, RF03 replacement). VS Code under protected still connects to an existing daemon.json daemon. Node has no portable process start-time API, so this stays a known gap, recorded for CQ-RF07.
- Persistent state, JetBrains changes, .moe edits, enabling verified-local.

Constraint: five test harnesses (daemon-start, daemon-json-cap, approval-paths, plan-approval-client, settings-wire) transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts alone with a closed require shim. Add no new local runtime import to MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, startDaemon spawns exactly [real node outside the project, real installed bundled/daemon/index.js, 'start', '--project', projectPath], with cwd = the installed daemon dir and an env without NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_PATH or relative/project PATH entries. Shown by tests in a new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs.

Under the protected profile, a missing installed daemon, or no acceptable node, spawns nothing, shows the 'Protected execution profile: … Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' refusal, and never consults the global-config daemon. Shown by tests.
The legacy profile behaves exactly as before: the existing daemon-start tests pass unchanged.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Reopen 2: QA qa-952969be failed DoD 1 again. First read rejectionDetails and Serena gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath.

How the leak works on a Windows host:
- Node namespaces fs paths with \\?\, so realpathSync.native('<project>.') gives ENOENT.
- isOutsideProject then falls back to a lexical compare and keeps the entry.
- libuv's PATH search and CreateProcessW apply Win32 normalization: they strip the dot and run project executables.

The architect's native probe (node v24.16.0) found two more leaks under the same DoD:
- \\localhost\C$\<project> and \\127.0.0.1\C$\<project> also run project executables, because realpath keeps the UNC form. A JDK 17 probe shows JetBrains has the same gap, filed as task-526a2080.
- An absolute spawn of <project>.\x.exe through a literal sibling folder named 'project.' runs <project>\x.exe. Node's namespaced mkdir creates such a folder.

QA's repro scripts are D:\qa-rf06b-r2\trailing-dot.cjs and aliases.cjs. Read them, but never write to that folder.

TESTS FIRST, in moe-vscode/tests/protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs. Both tests must be RED before step 2. The spellings below are in Windows notation; write them as JS literals with escaped backslashes.

(a) A cross-platform predicate test for the new export isWindowsAlias(p, windows):
- windows=true answers true for: C:\p.  C:\p.\  C:\p.\bin  'C:\p. '  'C:\p .'  //?/C:/p.  //?/C:/p./bin  C:\PROJEC~1.  \\?\C:\p.  'C:\p \bin'  \\srv\sh  //srv/sh  \\?\UNC\srv\sh  \\localhost\C$\x
- windows=true answers false for: C:\p  C:\p\  C:\  'C:\Program Files\nodejs\'  C:\Python3.11\Scripts  \\?\C:\x
- windows=false answers false for: /tmp/p.  /tmp/p./bin  '/tmp/a /b'  //srv/sh
Leave out \.\ and \..\ rows: isOutsideProject applies the predicate to path.resolve forms, where those segments are already normalized.

(b) One native-Windows test, skipped elsewhere the same way as the rooted-spelling test. It uses fixture(t), with p = f.project.
- Setup: copy %SystemRoot%\System32\whoami.exe to p\moe-rf06b-alias.exe and to p\bin\moe-rf06b-alias.exe.
- The alias spellings:
  - p + '.', p + '.\', p + '.\bin', p + '. ' and p + ' .';
  - '//?/' + p with forward slashes + '.', with and without '/bin';
  - '\\localhost\' + p[0] + '$' + p.slice(2);
  - '\\127.0.0.1\' + p[0] + '$' + p.slice(2).
- isOutsideProject(alias, p) is false for each one, whether or not the admin share is reachable.
- protectedDaemonEnvironment({ PATH: [...aliases, f.outside].join(';'), SystemRoot }, p, f.node, true, undefined).PATH equals [path.dirname(f.node), f.outside].join(';').
- Control: require('node:child_process').spawnSync('moe-rf06b-alias', { cwd: f.outside, env: { PATH: p + '.', SystemRoot } }).status is 0. This shows the host really aliases the raw spelling, so the test is not vacuous.
- The same bare-name spawnSync with the filtered env gives error.code 'ENOENT'.
- Last, write(path.join(p + '.', 'node.exe')) creates a node file in a literal sibling 'project.' folder. plain(api.installedExecutable(that file, p)) deep-equals { rejected: 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path' }.
- Check that the fixture's fs.rmSync cleanup also removes the literal folder, leaving no moe-rf06b-* temp dir.

RED evidence. Record both outputs:
- Linux `cd moe-vscode && node --test tests/protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs` fails (a), because isWindowsAlias is undefined.
- `cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-vscode && node --test tests/protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs"` also fails (b) at isOutsideProject.

Implement in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, next to isFullyQualified. Add no import.

  /** Windows can read these as a local folder realpath cannot map back: Win32 strips a segment's trailing '.' or ' ' that Node's \\?\ fs keeps, and a UNC share can expose any local folder. */
  export function isWindowsAlias(p: string, windows = process.platform === 'win32'): boolean {
      return windows && (/[. ](?:[\\/]|$)/.test(p) || comparablePath(p, false).startsWith('//'));
  }

comparablePath already maps \\?\C:\x to C:/x, so device spellings of a local drive are not UNC, and it maps \\?\UNC\srv\sh and \\.\UNC\srv\sh to //srv/sh.

Use it in exactly two places, both with HOST semantics (the default parameter). Never pass the windows argument that tests use for env-key casing. Never hand the function itself to .some/.map, or the element index binds to `windows`.

1. isOutsideProject: after the isFullyQualified check, compute forms = pathForms(p) once, and return false when forms.some(form => isWindowsAlias(form)). The forms are the path.resolve spelling and, if it resolves, the realpath. This drops every alias spelling, and every mapped drive that resolves to a share, from protectedPathEntries, nodeOnProtectedPath and protectedDaemonEnvironment.
2. selectInstalledFile, after the regular-file check and before the root and project containment checks: if (isWindowsAlias(real)) { return rejected(`${label} is not a plain local Windows path`, real); }. The accepted real path is exactly what spawn and CreateProcessW receive: node, the daemon argument and its dirname cwd, and RF06's wrapper and proxy. So it must read the same under Win32 normalization.

Error handling:
- isWindowsAlias is a pure string test and never throws.
- isOutsideProject keeps its existing try/catch, so a realpath failure other than ENOENT (EACCES, a network error on an unreachable share) still answers false, never true.
- The new selectInstalledFile refusal goes through the existing rejected() helper: the log gets the absolute path, the UI gets the reason only, and startProtectedDaemon spawns nothing.

Refuse rather than canonicalize. Node has no GetFullPathName binding, and re-implementing Win32 normalization in JS would be new attack surface. Nothing can reliably map a share back to a local path.

This is deliberately stricter than JetBrains, which keeps an OUTSIDE '<dir>.' entry as written, because toRealPath normalizes it. Its UNC gap is task-526a2080. Every project spelling is refused here.

Accepted cost: under the protected profile on Windows, network-share PATH entries and a network node or extension install are not used. That fails closed.

Nothing else changes. These stay byte-identical: unquoted, protectedPathEntries, protectedDaemonEnvironment, startProtectedDaemon, the legacy code and the imports. On POSIX hosts, trailing dots and spaces stay literal name characters. Step 1's tests now pass on Linux and on native Windows.

Run the verification gate once, fresh, after step 2, on native Windows from WSL:
  cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes && cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile"
It must exit 0, and step 1's native-Windows alias test must be reported as passed, not skipped. Quote its ✔ line. This output is the complete_task verification evidence.

Also:
- Run Linux `cd moe-vscode && npm test`. It must exit 0; the Windows-only rows skip there.
- RF06's protected-runtime.test.cjs and the five legacy harnesses must pass unchanged.
- Re-run QA's repro logic against the working tree. Copy trailing-dot.cjs and aliases.cjs from D:\qa-rf06b-r2\ into a scratch dir outside the checkout, point them at the working-tree MoeDaemonClient.ts, and run them through cmd.exe. Expect 'NO LEAK', and kept:false on every aliases row.

Adversarial self-review of the reopen-2 diff only. Load adversarial-self-review. Check:
(a) Every QA spelling and every probe spelling is refused: \\localhost\<drive>$, \\127.0.0.1\<drive>$ and a literal '<project>.' folder.
(b) No accepted real path or kept PATH entry can read differently under Node's literal fs and under Win32 normalization. The gating comes only from process.platform.
(c) POSIX behavior is unchanged (the Linux run). No ordinary local Windows spelling is newly refused: C:\Program Files\nodejs\, dotted names such as Python3.11, and \\?\C:\ device forms.
(d) The legacy spawn options and messages are byte-identical. There is no new import, process.env is never mutated, and UI messages carry no absolute path.
(e) Each mutant below must be killed by an assertion:
- drop the check in isOutsideProject;
- drop the check in selectInstalledFile;
- remove ' ' from the character class;
- anchor the regex to the end of the path only;
- drop the UNC clause;
- ignore the windows parameter.

Report in the completion summary:
- The size: `git diff --numstat 0645f5e3^ -- moe-vscode/`. Today it is +400/-3, net 397.
  - Target reopen-2 growth: at most 45 net.
  - Ceiling: 460 net total, set by the pending CQ-RF06b size-only exception prop-3f719e10.
  - State whether that rail is active in get_context allRails.epic. Until it is, the governor holds REVIEW.
- The deliberate JetBrains divergences: an outside '<dir>.' entry and network-share entries are dropped. The JetBrains UNC follow-up is task-526a2080.
- What stays out of scope, shared with JetBrains: a not-yet-existing PATH leaf under a symlinked or 8.3 local ancestor, which is still compared lexically.

reopenReason:
DoD 1 still fails on native Windows, deterministically and with no race. A trailing '.' on a segment of an EXISTING project-dir spelling passes the protected PATH filter, and the OS reads it as the project. Node namespaces fs paths (\\?\), so realpath('<project>.') is ENOENT and isOutsideProject compares lexically and returns true. protectedDaemonEnvironment keeps the entry, and libuv's PATH search (Win32, no \\?\) strips the dot.

Repro on the committed source: `cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes && node D:\qa-rf06b-r2\trailing-dot.cjs"` exits 1, LEAK: 3. A bare-name spawn from the installed cwd with the filtered env ran the project's exe via '<project>.', '<project>.\bin' and '<project>. '. aliases.cjs adds '<project>.\', '//?/<project>.' and '<8.3>.'. This contradicts step-4's 'trailing-dot spellings of an EXISTING project dir are refused through realpath'. JetBrains refuses these through Java NIO toRealPath (JbParity.java probe), so parity fails too. Logs are in D:\qa-rf06b-r2\.

Verified OK:
- Delivery: 6d0a4451 (+ checkpoint 7a9a8194) is on moe/work-2026-10-24 and origin, and the tree matches the commit.
- The rooted/drive-relative fix holds.
- Recorded Windows gate exit 0: 286 tests, 282 pass, 4 skips, tsc ok. Linux: 285 pass, 1 skip.
- DoD 2, 3 and 4 hold.
- Net 397/400. Complexity pass: net 0.

DoD 1 has failed twice. The re-plan needs an RF06b size rail or its own slice, because a fix plus a test exceeds 400.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the protected execution profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension: the real bundled/daemon/index.js, run by a real node executable outside the project, with 'start' and cwd = the installed daemon dir. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH keeps only fully qualified entries outside the project, spelled as validated. On a Windows host, a Windows alias is never treated as outside the project and never accepted as an installed real path. A Windows alias is a path form with a segment ending in '.' or ' ' (Win32 strips those characters, but Node's \\?\-namespaced fs keeps them, so realpath cannot see the alias), or a UNC form (a share can expose a local folder, and realpath keeps the UNC form). Any rejection starts nothing and shows 'Protected execution profile: <reason>. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' The legacy profile is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: D1: the protected spawn has the exact command, args, cwd and env contents
D2: a missing installed daemon gives the exact refusal, no spawn, and never consults the global-config daemon or resolveDaemonRuntime
D3 and D4: the node rules (fully qualified, real, outside the project, in-process PATH lookup) are enforced, and the first candidate found is validated
D5 and D6: candidate order, and Windows case-insensitive env handling with a single PATH spelling
D7 and the existing harnesses: the legacy spawn is unchanged
Reopen 1 (kept): rooted and drive-relative Windows spellings are refused on any host drive
Reopen 2, predicate: isWindowsAlias(p, true) is true for segments ending in '.' or ' ' and for UNC forms, false for ordinary local and \\?\C:\ spellings, and false for every input with windows=false

Reopen 2, native Windows: every trailing-dot/space and loopback-UNC spelling of the EXISTING project is refused by isOutsideProject and dropped from the protected env PATH. A bare-name spawn of a project executable from an outside cwd with that env fails ENOENT, while the raw '<project>.' spelling runs it (control)
Reopen 2, native Windows: a node file in a literal sibling '<project>.' folder is refused with 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path'

The native-Windows gate cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes && cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile" exits 0 with the reopen-2 Windows test executed (not skipped), and Linux `cd moe-vscode && npm test` exits 0
invariants: Under protected, nothing is spawned unless both the daemon and node are accepted
Refusal messages carry reasons only; absolute paths go to the log
Every kept PATH entry and every accepted real path reads identically under Node's literal fs and under the Win32 normalization the OS applies to spawn and PATH search, and none is a UNC form
Host semantics: the Windows alias rule applies only when process.platform is win32, never through the windows argument tests pass on Linux for env-key casing
compatibility: The legacy profile keeps resolveBundledDaemonPath || resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath, resolveDaemonRuntime, 'init' with --name, and the exact spawn options {detached, stdio, windowsHide, env}
No new local runtime import in MoeDaemonClient.ts: five existing vm harnesses transpile it alone

Mirrors JetBrains protectedDaemonCommand, protectedDaemonEnvironment and applyDaemonPath semantics, apart from --host (VS Code has no WSL agent toggle). It is deliberately stricter on Windows: JetBrains keeps an OUTSIDE '<dir>.' entry as written (toRealPath normalizes it) and still keeps UNC entries; the latter is follow-up task-526a208079b5467db13cb9dd10da442e

On Windows, Node's fs resolves a path, then namespaces it with \\?\, which disables Win32 normalization: realpathSync.native('C:\p.') is ENOENT even when C:\p exists, while libuv's PATH search (GetFileAttributesW) and CreateProcessW strip the dot (QA and architect probes, node v24.16.0; Serena gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath)

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: QA offered a split or a size rail. A split is a dead end: DoD 1 needs the fix on this row, and QA measures the file diff since 0645f5e3^ (as with WT-S). So the fix lands in place with one size-only waiver, prop-3f719e10, following the RF01 and RF04 precedent. Refuse vs canonicalize: refuse. Node has no GetFullPathName binding, a JS re-implementation of Win32 normalization is new attack surface, and a share can't be mapped back to a local folder. UNC joined the scope after the architect probe: \\localhost\C$\<project> runs project executables in VS Code. It is the same DoD-1 class, a likely round-3 reject, and about 1 line to close. A walk-to-the-nearest-existing-ancestor canonicalization for not-yet-existing leaves was left out: QA accepted that gap as theoretical in round 2, and JetBrains shares it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Node's fs on Windows runs path.resolve, then toNamespacedPath (\\?\). '.' and '..' segments and separators are normalized; a trailing '.' or ' ' on a segment is not. libuv search_path (GetFileAttributesW) and CreateProcessW normalize, and Java toRealPath runs GetFullPathName first. realpathSync.native of a UNC spelling, even a loopback admin share, stays UNC, and so does Java toRealPath. selectInstalledFile serves installedArtifact (RF06's daemon, wrapper and proxy, also via AgentLauncher.ts) and installedExecutable (node). isOutsideProject feeds protectedPathEntries, which feeds nodeOnProtectedPath and protectedDaemonEnvironment. comparablePath strips the \\?\ and \\.\ device prefixes and maps \\?\UNC\x to //x.
planningNotes.risks:

- Host semantics only: tests pass windows=true on Linux, for env-key casing, with POSIX paths.
- The native-Windows test must really run in the gate, not skip. Quote its ✔ line.
- The control spawn needs SystemRoot in env. whoami.exe exists on every Windows SKU and on GitHub runners.
- The UNC rows hold whether or not admin shares are reachable: the lexical rule refuses them, and so does a non-ENOENT realpath error. Never assert a share-dependent spawn result for them.

- Size: net 397 today. Keep growth ≤45; the ceiling is 460 (prop-3f719e10). A size-only reject at reopen 2 burns the last reopen.

issues.description: DoD 1: Node's Windows realpath uses \\?\ paths (no Win32 normalization), so pathForms gets ENOENT for '<project>.', '<project>.\', '<project>.\bin', '//?/<project>.' and '<8.3>.' spellings of the EXISTING project. isOutsideProject (259) accepts them lexically; protectedPathEntries (285)/env (346) keep them; libuv PATH search strips the period and runs project exes. Keep only spellings the OS reads identically: refuse segments ending in '.' (consider ' ') or canonicalize as Win32 does.
